pathway.title: MasterBrand, Inc. — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage is high on every measure, and the issuer's own 4.3x is the most flattering of them. Net debt of USD 1,091.1 million is 5.16x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 211.6 million and 16.43x trailing reported EBITDA of USD 66.4 million, while the issuer's 4.30x divides by USD 253.9 million, which adds American Woodmark's full twelve months, about USD 42.3 million of it from before the merger on the release's own table. Net debt has nearly doubled from USD 559.1 million at the end of fiscal 2023 as two acquisitions added debt, while adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 363.6 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 211.6 million over the last twelve months, including American Woodmark since closing. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-1; calculation calc-2; calculation calc-16

Demand is weak across channels, and the decline is not a one-quarter event. Pro forma net sales of the combined business fell 4.83% in the third quarter and 7.86% over 39 weeks. Legacy MasterBrand sales fell in every channel over 39 weeks, with dealers down 5.4%, retailers down 3.3% and builders down 6.5%, while American Woodmark's own sales, implied by the pro forma table, fell faster at 13.09%. Management assumes no demand improvement through year end, with its addressable market down high-single digits, and customers are not required to buy any minimum amount, so volume can fall quickly; Lowe's and Home Depot took 33% of fiscal 2025 net sales. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 40; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 17; calculation calc-8; calculation calc-16

Margins have broken rather than dipped, because fixed production costs are spread over lower volume while inflation runs ahead of pricing, and the damage is in the legacy business: its adjusted EBITDA fell 46.7% to USD 140.2 million over 39 weeks, while American Woodmark has added USD 36.3 million at a 7.54% margin, close to the legacy 7.05%. Gross margin fell from 33.1% in fiscal 2023 to 30.3% in fiscal 2025 and was 24.6% in the third quarter of 2026 against 31.2% a year earlier, and 23.5% once USD 10.9 million of non-recurring duty refunds are removed. Production labor and overhead took 36.7% of net sales over 39 weeks against 33.3% a year earlier, and selling, general and administrative expenses rose from 20.9% to 24.4% of net sales between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1–2, 13; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 11, 30; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 73; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-9; calculation calc-10; calculation calc-18

Guidance implies that earnings fall by about a quarter in 2026 while sales rise by about a quarter. Fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 38 million to USD 48 million would bring 2026 to USD 214.5 million to USD 224.5 million, down 28.1% to 24.7% from fiscal 2025 on net sales up 25.4% to 26.4%, a margin of 6.26% to 6.49% against 10.9%. Free cash flow guided to about breakeven for the year implies a fourth-quarter outflow of about USD 43.6 million after USD 43.6 million generated in 39 weeks, and interest of about USD 24 million in the quarter takes roughly half or more of the guided earnings. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 10; calculation calc-6; calculation calc-7; calculation calc-9

Covenant headroom cannot be read, and the arithmetic points to little of it. The ceiling is 3.75x net leverage for the merger quarter and the three after it and 3.25x thereafter, with a minimum interest cover of 3.00x. Adding the stock-based compensation that the release names to the issuer's combined adjusted EBITDA gives USD 279.8 million and net leverage of 3.90x, so reported compliance rests on other permitted adjustments or a different net debt definition that the filings do not itemise. Interest cover on the same measure is 3.45x on trailing interest expense and 2.91x on the guided fourth-quarter interest run rate, and holding net debt flat the 3.25x ceiling needs USD 335.7 million of covenant earnings, USD 55.9 million more, which is close to the more than USD 50 million of synergy actions that management says it has initiated or completed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation calc-3; calculation calc-4; calculation calc-5

Liquidity buys time but does not fix the structure. Liquidity of USD 694.2 million is USD 139.7 million of cash and USD 554.5 million of revolver availability, the first quarter of 2026 needed USD 110.0 million of net revolver borrowing to fund a USD 146.2 million cash outflow, USD 18.8 million of Term Loan A falls due within twelve months, and the revolver and Term Loan A, USD 540.1 million drawn, mature together in June 2029 ahead of the USD 700.0 million 7.00% notes in July 2032. Refinancing needs leverage back near covenant levels by mid-2028, when the 2029 facilities become current, and market access was last shown in June 2024 before leverage rose. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 19–22; 10-Q_2026-03-29_mbc-20260329.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-12; calculation calc-13

Asset cover is thinner than book equity suggests, which weakens recovery for unsecured creditors. Goodwill and other intangibles of USD 2,202.6 million exceed equity of USD 1,963.6 million, leaving tangible equity of negative USD 239.0 million, and intangibles are 50.9% of assets. The 7.00% notes are unsecured while the credit agreement is secured on certain assets that the filings do not list, and operating lease liabilities of USD 287.9 million sit outside net debt. The market value of the shares fell below book net assets at times in 2026 and management judged that no impairment test was needed. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 16, 20; calculation calc-14

Financial policy has favoured growth by acquisition, but payouts to shareholders have stopped. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, so no outside owner is available to inject equity, the company does not expect to pay dividends in the short term and made no repurchases in 2026 after USD 18.1 million in fiscal 2025. The chief financial officer role is held on an interim basis after a separation agreement dated 2026-10-23, during integration and covenant testing. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 51; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-17

Operating levers exist and are being used, which supports the view that cash can be preserved. Capital expenditure was USD 78.2 million or 2.86% of net sales in fiscal 2025 and USD 36.6 million in 39 weeks of 2026, so spending can be cut, and management reports USD 11 million of synergies realised, actions for more than USD 50 million initiated or completed and a target above USD 100 million of annual run-rate savings by the end of year three. These are management statements, and restructuring charges of USD 33.1 million with acquisition-related costs of USD 48.4 million in 39 weeks show that savings cost cash first. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-11; calculation calc-17

runs.text: Five weaknesses outweigh four strengths in the current cycle; each item below runs from the evidence to the mechanism to the effect on creditors.

- Strength: scale and channel reach give the revenue base breadth. Management calls MasterBrand the largest residential cabinet maker in North America and describes the industry's largest dealer network, and dealers took 54.87% of fiscal 2025 net sales beside retailers and builders, so a cut by one channel can be partly absorbed. The size claim is management's own and no third-party ranking is supplied. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 7; calculation calc-17

- Strength: liquidity and a distant maturity wall give time. Liquidity of USD 694.2 million and no maturity before June 2029 beyond USD 18.8 million of Term Loan A amortization in the next twelve months mean the next test is a covenant, not cash, which gives management time to deliver savings. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; calculation calc-13

- Strength: spending can be cut and shareholder payouts have stopped, which preserves cash. Capital expenditure is 2.86% of net sales, no dividend is expected and no shares were repurchased in 2026, so cash that would leave the group is retained for debt service. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 49, 74–75; calculation calc-11; calculation calc-17

- Strength: the merger was paid for mainly in shares and lenders have shown willingness to adapt covenants. Of USD 1,059.8 million of consideration, USD 682.8 million was shares and USD 367.5 million was American Woodmark's debt refinanced by Term Loan A, so the equity base grew with the business, and the Second Amendment of 2026-03-26 shows lenders will negotiate. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 21; calculation calc-17

- Weakness: leverage and covenant headroom. Net debt is 5.16x trailing adjusted EBITDA and 3.90x on the reconstructed covenant measure against a 3.75x ceiling that steps down to 3.25x, so a small earnings miss can force an amendment, whose price and terms creditors bear. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation calc-1; calculation calc-3; calculation calc-4

- Weakness: margin sensitivity to volume. Production labor and overhead took 36.7% of net sales over 39 weeks and gross margin was 24.6% in the third quarter, so further volume loss removes earnings faster than costs can be cut. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 37; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation calc-9; calculation calc-10

- Weakness: customer concentration and credit risk. Lowe's and Home Depot took 33% of fiscal 2025 net sales with no minimum purchase commitments, and USD 17.8 million of receivables is reserved, including USD 17.1 million for one customer, so a retailer reset or a dealer failure hits cash directly. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation calc-16

- Weakness: thin free cash flow against a rising interest bill. Free cash flow is guided to about breakeven for 2026 and 43.6% of principal is floating, so each 100 bp adds USD 5.4 million a year while earnings are falling. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; calculation calc-7; calculation calc-13

- Weakness: asset cover. Intangibles are 50.9% of assets and tangible equity is negative USD 239.0 million, with the notes unsecured behind bank debt secured on certain assets, so recovery for noteholders depends on enterprise value rather than hard assets. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 20; calculation calc-14

Opportunities that could improve credit quality are cost synergies above USD 100 million of annual run-rate savings, a housing and remodeling recovery that restores volume against fixed costs, and growth in e-commerce sales. Threats that could weaken it are the cabinet tariff doubling on 2027-01-01, further volume loss at the two largest retailers, price competition from lower-cost imports and the covenant step-down in 2027. Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 6, 8, 15–17; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 34

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The merger with American Woodmark closed on 2026-05-28. Each American Woodmark share was converted into 5.15 MasterBrand shares, which made the former American Woodmark holders about 37% of the combined company, and the preliminary total consideration was USD 1,059.8 million, which includes the USD 367.5 million settlement of American Woodmark's existing debt. Purchase accounting recognised USD 197.2 million of goodwill and remains preliminary, so the acquired balances can still change. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 8–11

The new debt for the merger is a USD 375.0 million delayed-draw Term Loan A, committed under a First Amendment dated 2025-11-03 and drawn in full on 2026-05-28. It repaid American Woodmark's debt and covered fees, matures in June 2029 with the revolver, and requires quarterly payments from September 2026 set as a share of the commitment. It sits beside the USD 750.0 million revolver and the USD 700.0 million 7.00% senior notes due 2032 that were issued on 2024-06-27. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 19–22

A Second Amendment dated 2026-03-26 raised the maximum net leverage ratio to 3.75x, 4.00x and 3.75x for the quarters to the end of 2026 and lowered the minimum interest coverage ratio to 2.75x until the earlier of 2027-01-01 or the merger becoming effective. The amendment's thresholds ended when the merger became effective, and the original 3.75x test for a material acquisition then applied for the merger quarter and the three after it. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-05-05_q12026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2

Earlier, the July 2024 purchase of Supreme Cabinetry Brands cost USD 520.0 million in cash from GHK Capital Partners LP and was funded with cash and USD 430.0 million of borrowings under the revolver of the credit agreement signed with the June 2024 notes. The separation from Fortune Brands on 2022-12-14 left the issuer with no named parent or sponsor. Basis: 10-K_2024-12-29_mbc-20241229.htm.jsonl, page 100; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 43; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 3

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Business and governance fact pack for MasterBrand, Inc. (issuer id mbc-1941365) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. It covers the business, the transactions, ownership and control, the operating model, the governance and financial-policy record of the issuer and its consolidated subsidiaries. It builds on the source readiness findings listed below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MasterBrand is a widely held cabinet manufacturer with no named sponsor, and its May 2026 merger with American Woodmark added debt and integration risk to a business reliant on two retailers for a third of sales, so creditors depend on cost savings, not owner support.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Third-quarter net sales rose 48.3% to USD 1,036.8 million only because American Woodmark added USD 355.7 million, while legacy sales fell 2.5%. Governance evidence is thin: the proxy statement and the credit documents are not supplied, and the chief financial officer's separation was agreed on 2026-10-23.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Two retailers, Lowe's and Home Depot, took 33% of fiscal 2025 net sales and the ten largest customers about 50%, so one retailer's volume cut or reset moves fixed-cost absorption quickly. Gross margin fell to 24.6% in the third quarter from 31.2% a year earlier on lower volume, fixed-cost under-absorption, inflation ahead of pricing and American Woodmark's lower margin, which leaves the cost base little room for further volume loss. The merger changed the mix: builders were 22.63% of third-quarter net sales against 13.65% a year earlier, and retailers 35.73% against 30.32%.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The merger was an all-stock transaction for American Woodmark's holders, who took about 37% of the combined company, while USD 375.0 million of Term Loan A repaid USD 367.5 million of American Woodmark's debt. Equity therefore grew with the business, but debt came with it, and the acquired business has to deliver the savings management targets because the 3.75x net leverage test for the merger quarter and the three after it is measured on a definition in the credit agreement that is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Management reports USD 11 million of cost synergies realised, actions under way for more than USD 50 million, and a target of over USD 100 million of annual run-rate savings by the end of year three, beside a separate USD 30 million cost reduction programme announced in February 2026. These are management statements, not results, and the cash cost of reaching them is visible: restructuring charges were USD 11.1 million in the third quarter and acquisition-related costs USD 48.4 million in the 39 weeks.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Tariffs add a dated risk: the federal tariff on kitchen cabinets and vanities is 25% and scheduled to rise to 50% on 2027-01-01. Gross tariff costs run at about 5% to 6% of 2026 net sales and management expects to offset them in full on a run-rate basis by year end, which is an expectation, while refunds of earlier duties added USD 10.9 million to third-quarter gross profit and will not recur.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: No dividend is expected, share repurchases stopped in 2026 after USD 18.1 million in fiscal 2025, and no controlling shareholder or sponsor appears in the filings. The auditor gave clean opinions and effective internal control at the 2025 year end. Against that, the chief financial officer role is held on an interim basis after the separation agreement, American Woodmark is excluded from the 2026 internal control assessment, and the proxy statement that would show directors and holders is not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The sponsor and governance risk level is Medium. Acquisitive growth, a covenant reset in March 2026 and a leverage step-up weigh against it, while the absence of distributions and an equity-funded merger weigh for it; legal capacity for distributions, new debt and collateral moves is not established because the credit agreement and the indenture are not supplied. This is an analyst reading of the evidence, not a score.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest contrary evidence is that integration is reported ahead of schedule, the merger was funded mainly with shares, no distribution is planned and the issuer states that all debt covenants were met at 2026-09-27, which would argue for lower risk. Cost savings realised well above USD 11 million, or legacy sales stabilising, would strengthen that case. A further fall in legacy volumes, a loss of volume at either large retailer, or the tariff on cabinets rising to 50% without offset would weaken it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The merger with American Woodmark closed on 2026-05-28. Each American Woodmark share was converted into 5.15 MasterBrand shares, which made the former American Woodmark holders about 37% of the combined company, and the preliminary total consideration was USD 1,059.8 million, which includes the USD 367.5 million settlement of American Woodmark's existing debt. Purchase accounting recognised USD 197.2 million of goodwill and remains preliminary, so the acquired balances can still change.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The new debt for the merger is a USD 375.0 million delayed-draw Term Loan A, committed under a First Amendment dated 2025-11-03 and drawn in full on 2026-05-28. It repaid American Woodmark's debt and covered fees, matures in June 2029 with the revolver, and requires quarterly payments from September 2026 set as a share of the commitment. It sits beside the USD 750.0 million revolver and the USD 700.0 million 7.00% senior notes due 2032 that were issued on 2024-06-27.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: A Second Amendment dated 2026-03-26 raised the maximum net leverage ratio to 3.75x, 4.00x and 3.75x for the quarters to the end of 2026 and lowered the minimum interest coverage ratio to 2.75x until the earlier of 2027-01-01 or the merger becoming effective. The amendment's thresholds ended when the merger became effective, and the original 3.75x test for a material acquisition then applied for the merger quarter and the three after it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Earlier, the July 2024 purchase of Supreme Cabinetry Brands cost USD 520.0 million in cash from GHK Capital Partners LP and was funded with cash and USD 430.0 million of borrowings under the revolver of the credit agreement signed with the June 2024 notes. The separation from Fortune Brands on 2022-12-14 left the issuer with no named parent or sponsor.

Countervailing evidence is the equity funding of the merger, the absence of distributions and the issuer's covenant compliance statement. fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Fundamental credit analysis for MasterBrand, Inc. (issuer id mbc-1941365) as of 2026-11-18 under the credit snapshot pathway. It combines the business, financial and ownership evidence into a creditor view of strengths, weaknesses, the main downside path and the signals to monitor, for the issuer and its consolidated subsidiaries including American Woodmark from 2026-05-28. It builds on the source readiness, financial foundation and business and governance findings listed below.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MasterBrand's creditors now depend on merger savings arriving in a falling market, because net debt of USD 1,091.1 million is 5.16x trailing adjusted EBITDA and the fourth-quarter guidance leaves little earnings or cash flow to reduce it.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3, 13; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-1

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity of USD 694.2 million and no maturity before June 2029 make a payment default unlikely unless a covenant is breached, and the issuer reports compliance. Covenant headroom is the weak point: on the adjustments the issuer names, net leverage is 3.90x against a 3.75x ceiling, and the ceiling falls to 3.25x from the second quarter of 2027. Free cash flow is guided to about breakeven for 2026, so deleveraging depends on an earnings recovery or on lender relief.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2–3; calculation calc-3; calculation calc-4; calculation calc-6; calculation calc-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage is high on every measure, and the issuer's own 4.3x is the most flattering of them. Net debt of USD 1,091.1 million is 5.16x trailing adjusted EBITDA of USD 211.6 million and 16.43x trailing reported EBITDA of USD 66.4 million, while the issuer's 4.30x divides by USD 253.9 million, which adds American Woodmark's full twelve months, about USD 42.3 million of it from before the merger on the release's own table. Net debt has nearly doubled from USD 559.1 million at the end of fiscal 2023 as two acquisitions added debt, while adjusted EBITDA fell from USD 363.6 million in fiscal 2024 to USD 211.6 million over the last twelve months, including American Woodmark since closing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 13; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 3; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-1; calculation calc-2; calculation calc-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Demand is weak across channels, and the decline is not a one-quarter event. Pro forma net sales of the combined business fell 4.83% in the third quarter and 7.86% over 39 weeks. Legacy MasterBrand sales fell in every channel over 39 weeks, with dealers down 5.4%, retailers down 3.3% and builders down 6.5%, while American Woodmark's own sales, implied by the pro forma table, fell faster at 13.09%. Management assumes no demand improvement through year end, with its addressable market down high-single digits, and customers are not required to buy any minimum amount, so volume can fall quickly; Lowe's and Home Depot took 33% of fiscal 2025 net sales.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 11, 40; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 8, 17; calculation calc-8; calculation calc-16

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins have broken rather than dipped, because fixed production costs are spread over lower volume while inflation runs ahead of pricing, and the damage is in the legacy business: its adjusted EBITDA fell 46.7% to USD 140.2 million over 39 weeks, while American Woodmark has added USD 36.3 million at a 7.54% margin, close to the legacy 7.05%. Gross margin fell from 33.1% in fiscal 2023 to 30.3% in fiscal 2025 and was 24.6% in the third quarter of 2026 against 31.2% a year earlier, and 23.5% once USD 10.9 million of non-recurring duty refunds are removed. Production labor and overhead took 36.7% of net sales over 39 weeks against 33.3% a year earlier, and selling, general and administrative expenses rose from 20.9% to 24.4% of net sales between fiscal 2023 and fiscal 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Guidance implies that earnings fall by about a quarter in 2026 while sales rise by about a quarter. Fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA of USD 38 million to USD 48 million would bring 2026 to USD 214.5 million to USD 224.5 million, down 28.1% to 24.7% from fiscal 2025 on net sales up 25.4% to 26.4%, a margin of 6.26% to 6.49% against 10.9%. Free cash flow guided to about breakeven for the year implies a fourth-quarter outflow of about USD 43.6 million after USD 43.6 million generated in 39 weeks, and interest of about USD 24 million in the quarter takes roughly half or more of the guided earnings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Covenant headroom cannot be read, and the arithmetic points to little of it. The ceiling is 3.75x net leverage for the merger quarter and the three after it and 3.25x thereafter, with a minimum interest cover of 3.00x. Adding the stock-based compensation that the release names to the issuer's combined adjusted EBITDA gives USD 279.8 million and net leverage of 3.90x, so reported compliance rests on other permitted adjustments or a different net debt definition that the filings do not itemise. Interest cover on the same measure is 3.45x on trailing interest expense and 2.91x on the guided fourth-quarter interest run rate, and holding net debt flat the 3.25x ceiling needs USD 335.7 million of covenant earnings, USD 55.9 million more, which is close to the more than USD 50 million of synergy actions that management says it has initiated or completed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation calc-3; calculation calc-4; calculation calc-5

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity buys time but does not fix the structure. Liquidity of USD 694.2 million is USD 139.7 million of cash and USD 554.5 million of revolver availability, the first quarter of 2026 needed USD 110.0 million of net revolver borrowing to fund a USD 146.2 million cash outflow, USD 18.8 million of Term Loan A falls due within twelve months, and the revolver and Term Loan A, USD 540.1 million drawn, mature together in June 2029 ahead of the USD 700.0 million 7.00% notes in July 2032. Refinancing needs leverage back near covenant levels by mid-2028, when the 2029 facilities become current, and market access was last shown in June 2024 before leverage rose.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 19–22; 10-Q_2026-03-29_mbc-20260329.htm.jsonl, pages 3–4; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-12; calculation calc-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Asset cover is thinner than book equity suggests, which weakens recovery for unsecured creditors. Goodwill and other intangibles of USD 2,202.6 million exceed equity of USD 1,963.6 million, leaving tangible equity of negative USD 239.0 million, and intangibles are 50.9% of assets. The 7.00% notes are unsecured while the credit agreement is secured on certain assets that the filings do not list, and operating lease liabilities of USD 287.9 million sit outside net debt. The market value of the shares fell below book net assets at times in 2026 and management judged that no impairment test was needed.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Financial policy has favoured growth by acquisition, but payouts to shareholders have stopped. No sponsor or controlling holder is named, so no outside owner is available to inject equity, the company does not expect to pay dividends in the short term and made no repurchases in 2026 after USD 18.1 million in fiscal 2025. The chief financial officer role is held on an interim basis after a separation agreement dated 2026-10-23, during integration and covenant testing.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 49; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 51; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Operating levers exist and are being used, which supports the view that cash can be preserved. Capital expenditure was USD 78.2 million or 2.86% of net sales in fiscal 2025 and USD 36.6 million in 39 weeks of 2026, so spending can be cut, and management reports USD 11 million of synergies realised, actions for more than USD 50 million initiated or completed and a target above USD 100 million of annual run-rate savings by the end of year three. These are management statements, and restructuring charges of USD 33.1 million with acquisition-related costs of USD 48.4 million in 39 weeks show that savings cost cash first.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 3; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-11; calculation calc-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The strongest evidence against a cautious view is that lenders have been accommodating and the issuer reports compliance. Lenders agreed a Second Amendment in March 2026 that relaxed the tests until the merger took effect, the issuer states that all covenants were met at 2026-09-27, the credit agreement lets the issuer count American Woodmark's trailing earnings and stock-based compensation, and the issuer's own estimate puts the fair value of its debt at 97.9% of carrying value, which shows no sign of market stress. Liquidity of USD 694.2 million with no maturity before June 2029 means that a covenant amendment, not a cash shortfall, is the likeliest test for creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 19–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 2; calculation calc-13; calculation calc-15

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The view would improve if fourth-quarter adjusted EBITDA reached the top of the USD 38 million to USD 48 million range, free cash flow for 2026 finished above breakeven, a disclosed covenant ratio showed a clear cushion below 3.25x, or synergies realised rose well above USD 11 million. It would worsen on adjusted EBITDA below USD 38 million, a fourth-quarter outflow well above about USD 43.6 million, revolver drawings above USD 165.0 million without a seasonal explanation, a covenant amendment request, or the cabinet tariff rising to 50% on 2027-01-01 without an offset.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Five weaknesses outweigh four strengths in the current cycle; each item below runs from the evidence to the mechanism to the effect on creditors.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength: scale and channel reach give the revenue base breadth. Management calls MasterBrand the largest residential cabinet maker in North America and describes the industry's largest dealer network, and dealers took 54.87% of fiscal 2025 net sales beside retailers and builders, so a cut by one channel can be partly absorbed. The size claim is management's own and no third-party ranking is supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength: liquidity and a distant maturity wall give time. Liquidity of USD 694.2 million and no maturity before June 2029 beyond USD 18.8 million of Term Loan A amortization in the next twelve months mean the next test is a covenant, not cash, which gives management time to deliver savings.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength: spending can be cut and shareholder payouts have stopped, which preserves cash. Capital expenditure is 2.86% of net sales, no dividend is expected and no shares were repurchased in 2026, so cash that would leave the group is retained for debt service.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 49, 74–75; calculation calc-11; calculation calc-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Strength: the merger was paid for mainly in shares and lenders have shown willingness to adapt covenants. Of USD 1,059.8 million of consideration, USD 682.8 million was shares and USD 367.5 million was American Woodmark's debt refinanced by Term Loan A, so the equity base grew with the business, and the Second Amendment of 2026-03-26 shows lenders will negotiate.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness: leverage and covenant headroom. Net debt is 5.16x trailing adjusted EBITDA and 3.90x on the reconstructed covenant measure against a 3.75x ceiling that steps down to 3.25x, so a small earnings miss can force an amendment, whose price and terms creditors bear.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 20–21; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 13; calculation calc-1; calculation calc-3; calculation calc-4

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness: margin sensitivity to volume. Production labor and overhead took 36.7% of net sales over 39 weeks and gross margin was 24.6% in the third quarter, so further volume loss removes earnings faster than costs can be cut.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 30, 37; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; calculation calc-9; calculation calc-10

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness: customer concentration and credit risk. Lowe's and Home Depot took 33% of fiscal 2025 net sales with no minimum purchase commitments, and USD 17.8 million of receivables is reserved, including USD 17.1 million for one customer, so a retailer reset or a dealer failure hits cash directly.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness: thin free cash flow against a rising interest bill. Free cash flow is guided to about breakeven for 2026 and 43.6% of principal is floating, so each 100 bp adds USD 5.4 million a year while earnings are falling.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 19–22; calculation calc-7; calculation calc-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Weakness: asset cover. Intangibles are 50.9% of assets and tangible equity is negative USD 239.0 million, with the notes unsecured behind bank debt secured on certain assets, so recovery for noteholders depends on enterprise value rather than hard assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Opportunities that could improve credit quality are cost synergies above USD 100 million of annual run-rate savings, a housing and remodeling recovery that restores volume against fixed costs, and growth in e-commerce sales. Threats that could weaken it are the cabinet tariff doubling on 2027-01-01, further volume loss at the two largest retailers, price competition from lower-cost imports and the covenant step-down in 2027.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: MasterBrand makes stock, semi-custom and premium kitchen and bath cabinets in the United States, Canada and Mexico and sells them through dealers, retailers and builders to remodeling and new construction. The 2026 merger changed the mix: builders rose from 13.65% to 22.63% of third-quarter net sales and retailers from 30.32% to 35.73%, while dealers fell from 56.03% to 41.64%, so a larger share of sales now depends on new construction and on retail buyers. Combined-group customer shares are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 13; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 7, 8; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Ownership gives creditors no sponsor to lean on. MasterBrand has been independent since the spin-off from Fortune Brands in December 2022, no controlling shareholder is named, and former American Woodmark holders own 36.86% of the shares, so any equity support would have to come from the market, where the share price has at times valued the company below book net assets.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 3; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 9, 16; Business & governance (CP-1A); calculation calc-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue durability is weak in the current cycle. Sales follow remodeling and single-family construction, both weaker in 2026, and customers carry no minimum purchase obligation, so volume can fall without notice. Pricing power is limited: the release attributes the legacy decline to market weakness, adverse mix and trade-downs, with only tariff pricing supporting average selling prices, and sales are lowest in the first quarter while operating cash flow is typically higher in the second half, so a weak first quarter draws on the revolver as it did in 2026.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, page 1; 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, page 37; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 9, 17; calculation calc-12

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive forces cap pricing. Rivalry is intense with few barriers to entry, so price competition rises in downturns; two retailers hold buyer power; lower-cost foreign producers and e-commerce price transparency add pressure, while tariffs add cost for the issuer; and raw materials come from a number of sources, so supplier power is moderate and tariffs are the main cost channel. The consequence is that margins cannot be defended by price in a downturn, so cost savings and a volume recovery must carry deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Only trade policy and the housing cycle materially alter credit quality; other political, social and technological factors do not appear to be a primary credit driver based on the provided materials. The cabinet tariff is 25% and scheduled to reach 50% on 2027-01-01, gross tariff costs are about 5% to 6% of 2026 net sales and management expects to offset them fully by year end, which is an expectation, and refunds of earlier duties of USD 10.9 million lifted the third quarter and will not recur. Higher interest rates weigh on remodeling demand, which the annual report ties to consumers' reluctance to invest in their existing homes, and they raise the cost of the USD 540.1 million of floating-rate debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 34–35; EX-99.1_2026-11-05_q32026earningspressrelease.htm.jsonl, pages 1, 3; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, page 14; calculation calc-9; calculation calc-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margin resilience is low in the near term. Raw materials took 38.3% of net sales and production labor and overhead 36.7% over 39 weeks, against 35.1% and 33.3% a year earlier, and labor and overhead are 49.0% of cost of products sold, a base that does not fall in line with volume. Management has started a manufacturing network review that includes the closure of American Woodmark's Monterrey plant, and a headcount reduction in corporate functions, with restructuring charges of USD 33.1 million in 39 weeks, and margin can be defended only if volume stabilises or savings arrive faster than inflation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 2, 23, 30; calculation calc-10; calculation calc-17

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Free cash flow conversion has weakened. Free cash flow was 58.1% of adjusted EBITDA in fiscal 2024, 39.4% in fiscal 2025 and 45.4% over the last twelve months, and in 39 weeks of 2026 it was USD 43.6 million against USD 65.0 million. Payables added USD 41.0 million in the 39 weeks, so operating cash flow leaned on supplier timing that can reverse, and cash interest paid rose to USD 78.6 million over the last twelve months from USD 41.7 million in fiscal 2024.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 3, 22; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 74–75, 106; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-11

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The capital structure is bank debt and one bond. Principal is USD 1,240.1 million: Term Loan A USD 375.1 million, the revolver USD 165.0 million and the USD 700.0 million 7.00% notes, of which 43.6% floats, so each 100 bp adds USD 5.4 million a year of interest, and no interest rate hedge is described in the filings supplied. Adjusted EBITDA covered cash interest 2.69x over the last twelve months and reported EBITDA 0.84x, against 4.01x and 2.88x in fiscal 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-27_mbc-20260927.htm.jsonl, pages 16, 19–22; 10-K_2025-12-28_mbc-20251228.htm.jsonl, pages 73, 106; Financial foundation (CP-1); calculation calc-13

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over the next two years the direction for credit quality is negative to stable at best. Management guides the fourth quarter to net sales of USD 958 million to USD 988 million and assumes no demand improvement through year end, the cabinet tariff step-up and the covenant step-down both fall in the first half of 2027, and duty refunds that lifted the third quarter will not recur. Tailwinds are the synergy programme, with second-half savings expected above about USD 15 million, and a legacy business that management says gained share.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Over three to five years the outcome turns on savings above USD 100 million of annual run-rate by the end of year three, which falls within weeks of the June 2029 maturities, so refinancing will be judged on realised rather than targeted savings. A housing and remodeling recovery would let volume absorb fixed costs and would lift cash flow before any savings, while higher rates or a longer downturn would raise the cost of the floating debt and delay deleveraging.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The issuer-specific downside begins with demand staying down through 2027 while the cabinet tariff doubles on 2027-01-01 and the offset arrives late. The first break would come in the first quarter of 2027, the seasonally weakest, when volume falls again against fixed production costs that took 36.7% of net sales in 2026 and savings realised are still only USD 11 million. Earnings would then track the low end of the fourth-quarter range of USD 38 million, free cash flow would turn negative, and the first quarter would again need revolver borrowing: in 2026 it needed USD 110.0 million of net borrowing on a USD 146.2 million cash outflow, and the larger combined working capital base makes a higher draw plausible.

fields.value: Overall, MasterBrand presents an adequate business profile supported by scale, channel breadth and liquidity, but credit quality is constrained by net leverage of 5.16x trailing adjusted EBITDA, compressed margins and thin covenant headroom. Cash-flow durability appears weak because free cash flow is guided to about breakeven for 2026 and conversion fell from 58.1% to 39.4% of adjusted EBITDA between fiscal 2024 and fiscal 2025. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on synergy delivery by mid-2028, on lender willingness to amend covenants and on a housing recovery. The primary downside path is a weak first half of 2027 that pushes covenant leverage above the ceiling before savings arrive. Further analysis would require the credit agreement, covenant compliance reports, American Woodmark's earlier statements and market pricing. Top risk: covenant leverage above the ceiling in 2027 before synergies are realised.
